summary:
We built Next Stop: Deep Space, a game where students design a spacecraft and fly it on a mission to the Moon. Players choose a question they want to investigate, such as whether there’s ice near the lunar south pole. They pick instruments, check what their rocket can carry, and decide how to spend their budget.
Once in orbit, players find out how well their design works. A spacecraft might collect plenty of measurements but have a weak antenna. When the Moon blocks its signal, some of that data is still on board. After the flight, players can swap the antenna and try again to see whether more data reaches Earth. It gives player a way to test an engineering idea for themselves, even if they’ve never studied spacecraft design.
details:
We built Next Stop: Deep Space so player can design a lunar mission and see how their choices affect the flight. Players can fit a camera to map the surface, a spectrometer to look for signs of ice, or radar to study underground layers. Solar panels supply power in sunlight, batteries keep instruments running in shadow, and antennas send measurements home. Each part adds weight and cost, so players must also choose a rocket that can carry their design and an orbit that reaches their target. After launch, players have 16 turns to collect and return data. They can replay a mission with one change, such as a larger battery, and see whether it helped.

We built the game in Godot using GDScript and modeled the astronaut in Blender. NASA’s LCROSS mission informed the ice survey. OpenAI Codex helped with coding, testing, and environment models.
